=== POLLER STALL ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (client + daemon) + TRANCHE-2 COMPLETE ===

THE #1 ISSUE IS SOLVED — and it was NOT a wedged tokio task. Root-caused by inspecting a frozen agent's live /control/status response:

ROOT CAUSE: a verbose agent's bro_status response (per-event payloads, even with the existing 2KB/string cap) exceeds the daemon's global 80KB MCP response cap (server/response.rs::cap_response_text), which BYTE-TRUNCATES the body mid-JSON-string and appends "[... response truncated to 80KB]". That corrupts the JSON. The cockpit's get_json→parse_tool_result_json then falls back to {"text":...}, update_daemon_task finds no status, and the row SILENTLY FREEZES (a finished agent shows "Active" forever; a running one freezes). The daemon is healthy (15ms /control/status), the poller task is alive, the render thread is alive — nothing panics or times out, so A2 catch_unwind and the supervisor heartbeat can't catch it. Measured: deepseek-v4 status = 88KB at tail=80 (truncated), 47KB at tail=40 (clean).

FIX CHAIN (all committed+pushed on beta):
- DAEMON (proper fix, cf87a52): task_status_json now bounds recentEvents by SERIALIZED SIZE (56KB budget, newest-first, ≥1 event) on top of the tail count, so /control/status + MCP bro_status are ALWAYS valid JSON under the cap regardless of requested tail. REDEPLOYING NOW.
- CLIENT (band-aid, 7b63f06/28384f5): poll tail 200→40 (under cap for verbose agents seen); surface an unparseable/truncated status LOUDLY (log + agent stderr) instead of silently no-op'ing.
- RECONCILE robustness (d8138a1): parse_daemon_status extracts status explicitly; missing/unparseable ⇒ inconclusive ⇒ optimistic poller, never terminal (was stranding live agents as Interrupted when a probe got a truncated response).
- POLLER-SUPERVISOR (c011dd3): last_poll_ms heartbeat + a watchdog that respawns any non-terminal task's poller if its heartbeat goes >30s stale. (Doesn't fix THIS bug — the poller wasn't wedged — but is the right backstop for genuine task death.)

OPERATIONAL DISCOVERY: my tmux Ctrl+Q+relaunch cycles were SPAWNING ORPHAN cockpit processes without killing the old ones — found TWO bro fleet procs (the original installed binary from session start + a /tmp/ct build) DUELING over the same fleet store (both reconcile/poll/persist), which corrupted the display state and made my cockpit "validations" unreliable for a stretch. === CORRECTION on the cockpit-logging follow-up (root cause pinned) ===

Isolated test (BRO_HOME=/tmp/lt bro fleet, no TTY): init_cockpit_logging DOES run — it created logs/cockpit.<date>.log — but the file is 0 bytes. So NOT an early-return/build failure (my earlier guess). The rolling file appender BUFFERS and only flushes on buffer-fill (~8KB) or process exit. The daemon logs at high volume so it auto-flushes; the cockpit emits only a handful of reconcile/poller lines per run, which stay buffered and never hit disk live (the 17 lines that DID appear flushed when earlier cockpit processes exited). Net: cockpit diagnostics are effectively write-on-exit, useless for live tailing while debugging.

FIX (follow-up, bro-only rebuild): swap the blocking rolling appender for tracing_appender::non_blocking(appender) and hold the returned WorkerGuard for the cockpit's lifetime (return it from init_cockpit_logging up to run()/run_agent so it isn't dropped) — non_blocking flushes on its own worker. Alternatively wrap with an explicit periodic flush. Low-risk, observability-only; deferred (the poller-stall bug it would have helped diagnose is already fixed).
